KJV Cambridge Paragraph Bible, eBible.org, https://ebible.org/engkjvcpb/

The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this
translation):
> "KJV Cambridge Paragraph Bible
The King James Version or Authorized Version of the Holy Bible, Cambridge Paragraph Bible edition
Public Domain
Language: English

Letters patent issued by King James with no expiration date means that to print this translation in the United Kingdom or import printed copies into the UK, you need permission. Currently, the Cambridge University Press, the Oxford University Press, and Collins have the exclusive right to print this Bible translation in the UK. This royal decree has no effect outside of the UK, where this work is firmly in the Public Domain. Please see http://www.cambridge.org/about-us/who-we-are/queens-printers-patent and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_James_Version#Copyright_status for more information."

Why this is public domain:
The Cambridge Paragraph Bible was first published in 1873-1879 in the United Kingdom; F. H. Scrivener, who prepared it, died in 1891 (Wikidata), so it is public domain in the United Kingdom (its country of origin) and in the United States. eBible.org notes that the United Kingdom letters patent over printing the KJV is a printing monopoly, not a copyright.

The read-aloud archive holds the Bible text chapter by chapter as plain
text, a front file, the copyright page (copr.htm, left out of the source),
and eBible.org's signing key (keys.asc, left out).

Sources of these facts: eBible.org's details page
(https://ebible.org/details.php?id=engkjvcpb) and the edition's own files.

held_out_by.note: eBible's chapter files, <code>_<NNN>_<BOOK>_<CC>_read.txt, are held out by book and chapter, so the same chapter is held out in every translation at once (maintainer's decision, 2026-10-23)

note: eBible.org rebuilds this zip often; the checksum covers the files inside, so a rebuild with the same text still matches.
